reason: Promote to active. The mechanism is that scoped-looking shell pre-approvals actually permit arbitrary execution, and unpinned MCP declarations in shared configs open a supply-chain path. It rests on a primary empirical scan of 3,171 public repos (arXiv 2609.07360, revised as v3 on 2026-09-25). Official Claude Code permissions docs independently confirm that Bash(cmd:*) is a trailing wildcard and that argument-constraining Bash rules are fragile and not a security boundary. The two sources agree. v3 corrected the broad-exec figure from 3.1% to 2.5%, which changes prevalence but not the mechanism. RMD-AGENTCFGPIN-001 is a current candidate remedy.

evidence.summary: 3,171 repos; 9.8% unpinned MCP, 3.8% skill shell pre-approval; v3 revised broad exec grants to 2.5%; validated prevalence 18.4% vs 25.5% raw.
Bash(cmd:*) is a trailing wildcard; argument-constraining patterns are fragile; allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly exists.
candidate; review shared agent config by effective capability and exact pinned version; OS sandbox as containment independent of rule strings.
